Rspo1 and Fezf2 are the L4 and L5 markers considered in the layer-boundary assessment. The retained panel is the Bregma approximately +1.0 MERFISH spatial display of IT cells expressing the two genes, using the panel’s stated z-scored expression encodings.

## Methods: layer-boundary and spatial-overlap assessment

The panel shows the same coronal slice as Extended Data Fig. 10a, highlighting L4/5 IT 5, L5 IT 1 and L5 ET cells. The related method defines spatial overlap as overlap of the corresponding cell-density distributions; the crop retains the observed spatial cell-type layout rather than the excluded overlap line plot in 10c.

**Source:** paper.pdf physical pp. 11-12, ‘Layer boundary assessment’; Extended Data Fig. 10 legend

panels.caption: Dendrogram showing the hierarchical relationship among the 39 glutamatergic, 42 GABAergic, and 14 non-neuronal clusters identified by MERFISH, constructed based on the z-scored cluster expression profiles and coloured by the subclass that each cluster belongs to (top). panels.methods:
## Methods: cell clustering analysis of MERFISH data

The taxonomy derives from the processed MERFISH cell-by-gene matrix and the resulting cluster/subclass assignments. The panel’s dendrogram uses z-scored cluster expression profiles and its dotplot displays subclass markers; it is not a classifier-performance matrix.

**Source:** paper.pdf physical pp. 10-11, ‘Cell clustering analysis of MERFISH data’; Extended Data Fig. 2 legend

panels.caption: Heatmap quantifying the anterior–posterior distribution of the neuronal clusters in the entire imaged region including the MOp and its adjacent areas. Slices were arranged from anterior-most to posterior-most based on their Bregma coordinates (Bregma +2.5 to −0.8). For each cluster, the fraction of cells found in each slice was determined and normalized to the maximum across all slices.
panels.methods:
## Methods/legend: serial-slice anterior-posterior distribution

The panel aggregates neuronal-cluster observations across serial coronal slices from Bregma +2.5 to −0.8. For each cluster, the fraction of cells in each slice was calculated and normalized to that cluster’s maximum across slices, yielding the displayed all-cells anterior-posterior heatmap.

**Source:** paper.pdf physical p. 2, MERFISH measurements on coronal slices at approximately 100-μm intervals; paper.pdf physical p. 21, Extended Data Fig. 4 legend

panels.methods:
## Methods: cell clustering and CCF registration

MERFISH-derived cell-by-gene profiles were normalized, reduced by PCA and clustered with Scanpy Louvain community detection; the figure displays the resulting cluster identities in a Bregma approximately +0.9 coronal slice. The grey MOp context comes from registration of MERFISH images to Allen CCF v3, not from a separate raw-tissue panel.

**Source:** paper.pdf physical pp. 10-11, ‘Cell clustering analysis of MERFISH data’ and ‘Registration to the Allen Reference Atlas and the common coordinate framework’; Fig. 1 legend

panels.methods:
## Methods: cell clustering analysis of MERFISH data

The MERFISH cell-by-gene matrix was preprocessed, z-scored, reduced to principal components and clustered. For presentation, UMAP embedded cells in two dimensions using the same principal components used for clustering; this panel selects L5 ET, L5/6 NP, L6 CT and L6b cells and colours them by cluster identity.

**Source:** paper.pdf physical pp. 10-11, ‘Cell clustering analysis of MERFISH data’; Fig. 2 legend

panels.label: Fig. 3e
panels.caption: Normalized expression of differentially expressed genes of all IT neurons across cortical depth. Here, differentially expressed genes refer to genes of which the expression varied substantially with cortical depth (Methods). Individual IT neurons were sorted in the order of ascending cortical depth and the genes were sorted by the cortical depth at which they exhibit maximal expression. The coloured bar at the bottom indicates the cluster identity of the cell, coloured as in a.
panels.methods:
## Methods: cortical-depth gene-gradient heatmap

IT-cell expression profiles were z-scored, cells were split into 50 equal cortical-depth bins, and genes whose mean normalized expression differed by more than 0.5 between any two bins were selected. Heatmap genes were ordered by depth of maximal expression and cells by normalized cortical depth.

**Source:** paper.pdf physical p. 12, paragraph beginning ‘To identify genes that vary as a function of the cortical depths of the IT cells’; Fig. 3 legend

papers.title: Spatial multi-omics at subcellular resolution via high-throughput in situ pairwise sequencing

panels.label: Extended Data Fig. 10a
panels.caption: Co-detection of 30 immune related proteins with 6 diagnostic marker genes mRNAs in human diffuse large B cell lymphoma (DLBCL) sections. The images for DAPI staining and oligo-dT-CY3 hybridization were illustrated in the right lower panel which are used for cell segmentation.
panels.methods:
## MiP-seq for in situ RNA detection

Padlock and initiator probes anneal adjacent to a target RNA; SplintR ligation closes the padlock, phi29 rolling-circle amplification creates an RCP, and pairwise sequencing by ligation reads dual-barcode combinations over one or more imaging rounds. Leica confocal or THUNDER imaging records DAPI and four fluorescence channels before computational decoding.

**Source:** paper.pdf Methods, physical pages 12–13

## Image registration; candidate-spots calling; decoding

For multi-round high-throughput data, z lengths are resized, later rounds are affinely registered to round 1 with SimpleElastix after white-top-hat/Gaussian preprocessing, channels are intensity-balanced, h-maxima calls candidates, and three-round/four-channel intensities are filtered and matched to the gene codebook.

**Source:** paper.pdf Methods, physical pages 14–15

## Cell segmentation and genes assignment

Images are z-projected; DAPI, oligo-dT-Cy3 or the average signal image supplies the segmentation reference. After sigmoid adjustment, Cellpose masks are manually corrected in Napari where necessary. An iterative KD-tree nearest-cell procedure assigns decoded spots within a distance threshold and excludes spots outside cell boundaries.

**Source:** paper.pdf Methods, physical page 15

## Co-detection of proteins, mRNAs and DNA

Antibodies are conjugated to oligonucleotides and decoded through the MiP-seq nucleotide workflow. Protein–RNA experiments add a T4-ligase step after SplintR; the PK-15 panels combine viral condition, proteins and eight cytokine/chemokine mRNAs, while DLBCL sections combine 30 antibody tags with six diagnostic mRNAs.

**Source:** paper.pdf Methods, physical pages 13–14

Bottom: Detailed views of four representative clusters linked to marker genes of known phenotypic groups. Data is derived from 324 nodules across 6 topographically separated regions used for 10X Visium from a single RUBIX experiment with two animals.
panels.methods:
## 10X Visium for FFPE spatial transcriptomics

Manual Visium FFPE or CytAssist workflows were applied to H&E-imaged sections with mouse transcriptome probe set v1. Libraries were sequenced on NovaSeq 6000 (four samples per 100-cycle SP flow cell; target 250 million reads per sample), and FASTQ/alignment processing used Space Ranger 2.0.1. Twelve datasets were generated; ML_II_B_2Cyt was excluded downstream because tissue detached.

**Source:** paper.pdf Methods, physical page 12

## Nodule annotation

Pathologists first annotated nodules from H&E in QuPath and 10X Loupe Browser. Annotation was refined with transcript expression in Loupe, as illustrated by Supplementary Fig. 3; normal regions were chosen 250–700 µm from tumours. Serial-section matches were manually reconciled.

**Source:** paper.pdf Methods, physical page 14

## Barcode expression pre-preprocessing

Spots were filtered at more than 5,000 UMIs and outer CytAssist spots were excluded. Barcode counts were normalized to 10,000 counts per spot and log(1p)-transformed; spatial views additionally use quantile rescaling as stated in the captions.

**Source:** paper.pdf Methods, physical page 14

## Bayesian modelling of perturbation probabilities from barcode counts

Barcode counts are modelled with a negative-binomial likelihood whose mean combines spot sensitivity, nodule membership, plasmid-to-barcode links, barcode expression rates and additive barcode noise. Per-nodule copy number has a six-order Dirichlet state; perturbation presence is 1 minus the posterior probability of zero copies. Pyro stochastic variational inference runs for 10,000 steps.

**Source:** paper.pdf Methods, physical pages 14–15

## Genotype-to-phenotype GLM and inference

Perturbation probabilities are explanatory variables in Bayesian GLMs for binary nodule-level IHC or non-zero spot-level gene counts. Spot sensitivity is propagated from the perturbation model; perturbation weights use Laplace priors. Pyro mean-field inference uses 2,000 gradient steps, and panels report posterior means with 3σ intervals.

**Source:** paper.pdf Methods, physical page 15

## Reading Visium Space Ranger output into data objects

Anndata/SingleCellExperiment objects were processed with Scanpy, Squidpy and scater and exchanged with ZellKonverter. Analysis retained the 19,464 features shared across all eleven usable slides; downstream phenotype work selected marker-associated genes and highly variable genes.

**Source:** paper.pdf Methods, physical page 16

## Extended Data Figure 10c display construction

Fit the paper's gene-level Bayesian GLM to the six primary regions (324 nodules) and 19,464 shared features. The top heatmap retains exactly the 1,283 genes having at least one significant perturbation feature weight, where significance means the posterior mean's 3σ interval excludes zero. It displays the fitted perturbation feature weights and orders the 1,283 genes by a one-dimensional UMAP embedding of their weight profiles. The lower panels are detailed views of four representative clusters associated with known phenotype marker groups.

**Source:** paper.pdf, physical pp. 9, 15–16 and 35; Extended Data Fig. 10 legend and `Genotype-to-phenotype GLM and inference`

## Frozen-corpus panel selectors exposed to the agent

- Use the six primary regions/324 nodules, 19,464 shared features, and the staged phenotype/marker definitions.
- Reconstruct perturbation probabilities and gene-level GLM coefficients from the composed counts; do not read Zenodo's derived joint/new_geno/probability members or the publisher coefficient matrix as inputs.

**Source:** frozen input mapping review based on the full paper, captions, Methods, staged-file schemas and public data records

# Relevant Methods

Source: user-supplied PDF, physical pages 15-16. Text extracted verbatim; equations may have PDF reading-order artifacts; consult the supplied PDF for equation layout.

Gene expression quantification per cell. We calculated normalized expression log 
counts for each cell using scran’s logNormCounts function108, with size factors 
corresponding to the total number of mRNAs (excluding the sex-specific gene Xist) 
identified for each cell. Size factors were scaled to unity, and a pseudocount of 1 
was added before the log counts were extracted. For the majority of downstream 
analyses, such as differential gene expression, we specifically included biological 
and technical variables (that is, z slice and FOV) as covariates. However, for 
the task of harmoniously visualizing gene expression in spatial coordinates, we 
extracted ‘batch-corrected expression’ values for each gene. This was done by first 
performing batch correction using the MNN method, implemented with fastMNN 
in the scran package108, with batch variables corresponding to z slice and FOV. 
For interpretable visualization, for each gene, we extracted the reconstructed 
expression values following batch correction and rescaled these to correspond to 
the distribution of expression values before batch correction.

Joint analysis with Gastrulation atlas. We downloaded the E8.5 Pijuan-Sala 
et al.6 10x Genomics scRNA-seq dataset from the Bioconductor package 
MouseGastrulationData and performed batch-aware normalization using the 
multiBatchNorm function in the scran package108 before extracting cells that 
correspond to a known cell type with at least 25 cells. Cell types associated with 
the somitic and paraxial mesoderm were further refined using labels assigned 
by Guibentif et al.118 (personal communication); blood subtypes (erythroid 1, 
erythroid 2 and erythroid 3 and blood progenitors 1 and 2) were collapsed to 
the two major groups, ExE mesoderm was renamed to lateral plate mesoderm 
and pharyngeal mesoderm was renamed to splanchnic mesoderm. Subsequently, 
only genes probed by both the scRNA-seq and seqFISH assays were kept for this 
analysis. We then jointly embedded the normalized log counts of each of the 
two datasets by performing batch-aware PCA with 50 components (excluding 
the sex-specific gene Xist) via the multiBatchPCA function in scran, with batch 
variables corresponding to sequencing runs in the Gastrulation atlas and FOV and 
z slice for the seqFISH data. We corrected for platform- and batch-specific effects 
using the MNN method (fastMNN55), ensuring that merge ordering is such that 
Gastrulation atlas batches are merged first (ordered by decreasing number of cells). 
This joint embedding of the Gastrulation atlas and seqFISH dataset was further 
reduced in dimension using UMAP, implemented by calculate UMAP in scran108, 
to allow the data to be visualized in two dimensions.
Cell type identification. To assign a cell-type label to each seqFISH cell, we 
considered the Gastrulation atlas cells that it was closest to in the batch-corrected 
space. We considered the k-nearest cells, with the distance from the seqFISH cell to 
its Gastrulation atlas neighbors being computed as the Euclidean distance among 
all of the batch-corrected PC coordinates. We set the number of nearest neighbors, 
k, to 25. Ties were broken by favoring the cell type of those closest in distance to 
the query cell. We calculated a ‘mapping score’ for each query cell as the proportion 
of the majority cell type present among the 25 closest cells.
To further refine the predicted cell types, we performed joint clustering of the 
Gastrulation atlas and seqFISH cells by building a shared nearest neighbor network 
on the joint PCs followed by Louvain network clustering. Additionally, we further 
subclustered the output by building a shared nearest neighbor network on the 
cells corresponding to each cluster followed by Louvain network clustering. We 
then inspected the relative contribution of cells to each subcluster as well as the 
expression of marker genes to identify subclusters that potentially required manual 
reannotation, either due to small differences in composition in the reference 
atlas or in the gene expression profile (Extended Data Fig. 3). We also identified 
a set of subclusters that were likely associated with low-quality cells, defined by 
lower total mRNA counts. Furthermore, we performed virtual dissection on 
regions corresponding anatomically to the developing gut tube and for these cells 
reclassified those that were ‘Surface ectoderm’ as ‘Gut tube’.

# Relevant Methods

Source: user-supplied PDF, physical pages 15-16. Text extracted verbatim; equations may have PDF reading-order artifacts; consult the supplied PDF for equation layout.

Cell neighborhood network construction. To construct a cell neighborhood 
network, for each cell within a given embryo and z slice, we extracted the 
polygon representation of the cell’s segmentation corresponding to a set of vertex 
coordinates. We then calculated an expanded segmentation by constructing a new 
polygon where each expanded vertex was lengthened along the line containing 
the original vertex and the center of the polygon. We performed a multiplicative 
expansion of 1.3 for each vertex. To construct the cell neighborhood network, 
we then identified the other cells in which segmentation vertices were found to 
be within the expanded polygon. Cell neighborhood networks were considered 
separately for each embryo and z slice combination.

Cell–cell contact map inference. We constructed cell–cell contact maps for multiple 
cell annotation labelings, including mapped cell types, subclusters within each 
cell type and mapped gut tube subtypes. To do this, for each embryo and z 
slice combination, we extracted the cell neighborhood network and cell-level 
annotation. We then generated cell–cell contact maps by first calculating the 
number of edges for which a particular pair of annotated groups was observed. 
We then randomly reassigned (500 times) the annotation by sampling without 
replacement and calculated the number of edges for all pairs of annotated groups. 
To construct the cell–cell contact map, we reported the proportion of times the 
randomly reassigned number of edges was larger than or equal to the observed 
number of edges. Small values correspond to the pair of annotation groups being 
more segregated, and large values correspond to them being more integrated in 
physical space than a random allocation. To combine these cell–cell contact maps 
for each embryo and z slice combination, we further calculated the element-wise 
mean for each pair of cell labels. We visualized this in a heat map, ordering the 
annotation groups using hierarchical clustering with Euclidean distance and 
complete linkage. In the case of the gut tube subtypes, we ordered these classes by 
the anterior–posterior ordering given by Nowotschin et al.2. In the brain subtypes, 
we ordered these classes by their approximate anatomical location, from the 
forebrain to the hindbrain region.

## User-supplied Fig. 2d method clarification (2026-09-09)

This clarification is supplied by the benchmark user, not extracted from author
analysis code by the benchmark. Apply it in preference to the contradictory
inequality sentence in the published Methods. Implement the analysis independently.

1. Construct one cell-contact graph per embryo x z slice. Use ordered segmentation
   polygon vertices, not centroid kNN, radius graphs or Delaunay triangulation.
   Expand each vertex radially about the polygon center by factor 1.3:
   v_expanded = center + 1.3 * (v_original - center).
2. Connect cells when another cell's original segmentation vertices lie inside
   the expanded polygon. This is the vertex-in-expanded-polygon heuristic
   (full = FALSE), not a generic polygon-intersection test. Treat contacts as an
   undirected graph, remove self-edges and duplicate edges; record conventions.
3. Count observed contacts for each pair of refined cell types. Hold the graph
   fixed, shuffle labels without replacement within each embryo x z slice,
   preserving type abundance. Perform 500 permutations per sample and record seed.
4. Compute S_ab = mean(C_observed_ab >= C_permuted_ab), including ties. This is an
   empirical percentile/rank, not an effect size or two-sided P value.
   0 = Segregated (blue), 0.5 = white, 1 = Integrated (pink).
   The Methods sentence describes the opposite inequality but its color/biology
   interpretation agrees with this user-supplied direction.
5. Average elementwise across the six embryo x z matrices, ignoring NA for absent
   types. At the final display stage exclude Low quality and cell types with total
   abundance <100. Cluster contact profiles with Euclidean distance and complete
   linkage and display the triangular contact heatmap.
6. The archived slice labels are z=2 and z=5 (the paper calls these selected layers
   1 and 2). Never mix embryos or slices in graph construction or permutations.

Data limitation: six of the 57,536 annotated cells have no polygon vertices in
either deposited representation (polygon_available=False). Do not invent their
boundaries. Report treatment of these cells explicitly; they cannot participate
in geometric contact inference. Refined labels are supplied as processed input
annotations, but no contact graph, contact matrix or author analysis code is given.

## Directed six-nearest-neighbour matrix and permutation test

Jointly infer 12 IRIS domains for the three patient-2 SCC slices P2_ST_rep1, P2_ST_rep2 and P2_ST_rep3 after retaining genes detected at more than five spots and spots with at least 100 UMI. Restrict the displayed analysis to P2_ST_rep2. For each retained location, find its six nearest spatial neighbours and record counts of their domain labels in an N × R matrix. For each focal domain, sum those rows to obtain the directed R × R domain-neighbour matrix. Each entry is therefore the number of times a location from the column domain occurs among the six nearest neighbours of a location in the row domain; do not symmetrize it or substitute a radius/hex-grid graph.

Run 1,000 permutations. In each, shuffle domain identities across locations without replacement while holding coordinates fixed, then reconstruct both matrices. For every ordered pair, the one-sided empirical P value is the fraction of permuted domain-neighbour entries that exceed the observed entry. Mark the panel only for P < 0.001.
